Tail rises nine points from the prior hour because the 31,254.75 high that was rejected an hour ago has been exceeded, a new record 31,280.00 has printed, and price holds roughly 10 points under that extreme. It stays inside the low band because the preceding 62.50-point retracement to 31,192.25 shows mean reversion still functions, and because SMH at +0.17% against a 0.71% gain in the cash index and a negative Dow make this a narrow megacap-led advance rather than a broad one-way wave. headline: Tail rises to 18% as the rejected 31,254.75 high gives way to a record 31,280.00, with price holding near the extreme against a 24-year-high 10-year yield
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 9% on a double-top rejection at 31,254.75 and named that unresolved level as the decisive evidence. That read has now been invalidated to the upside.

NQZ26 pushed through the rejected high and printed a new record 31,280.00. The last verified quote is 31,272.00 at 17:16:21Z, up 210.25 points or 0.68% on the 31,061.75 prior close, with a day range of 30,957.50 to 31,280.00 against a 31,059.00 open. Price is holding roughly 10 points beneath the extreme. The cash index confirms it: NASDAQ-100 is 31,028.04 at 17:26:24Z, up 220.11 points or 0.71%, with its own session high of 31,034.33 just six points above spot. Both the futures and the cash index are sitting at record levels rather than fading from them.

That sequence matters. An extreme was rejected, a 62.50-point retracement to 31,192.25 followed, and the market then extended through the rejection to a new high. Repeated extension after a failed retracement, combined with price holding near the session extreme, is the pattern that most reliably precedes a path which denies mean reversion, and it is why Tail moves up nine points.

Three things keep it inside the low band. First, the retracement was real: 62.50 points of two-way trade is not the shallow, failed pullback structure that defines a pathological path. Second, the advance is narrow. SMH is only +0.17% at 631.69 while the cash index gains 0.71%, so semiconductors are badly lagging the move, and the Dow is negative at -0.13%. Leadership is concentrated in NVDA at +1.1% with MSFT, META and TSLA each above +1%. Narrow megacap-only advances into a record close have historically produced chop rather than sustained one-way extension. Third, the cross-asset picture is in conflict rather than alignment: the 10-year is at 5.35%, up about six basis points and near its highest since 2002, with the long bond around 5.69% and a synchronised global long-end selloff behind it. Rising long rates are a direct valuation headwind to the equity bid, which is an unresolved tension and a Stress input, not a Tail amplifier.

Stress rises to 52% on that tension. September ISM services printed 54.9 against 55.4 prior, but the prices index rose to 74.0 from 72.6, its highest since July 2022, while business activity fell to 56.5 from 61.7. Softening activity alongside accelerating services prices, set against 24-year-high long yields and record equity valuations, is a genuinely difficult environment. It is offset for now by VIX at 15.48, sitting at its session low against a 16.38 high, and by WTI down 1.19% at 90.03, both of which argue against immediate volatility expansion.

Confidence holds at 88%. Current futures and cash quotes with timestamps, the full session range, VIX, both 2-year and 10-year yields, oil, verified September ISM services internals, megacap and semiconductor breadth and a verified seven-day calendar were all available. The shared Finviz context file was not usable this run: its latest publication is dated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly 5.8 days old and well outside the 90-minute freshness limit, with collection status partial. It was therefore excluded entirely and the assessment rests on independent research, which is the intended fail-open behaviour.

The remaining checkpoint today is power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, where closing imbalances around a record print are the main conditional amplifier. Tomorrow the August balance of trade at 12:30Z, Fed Williams at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Fed Bowman at 14:45Z form the next cluster.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 17:00Z contain 23 published Claude assessments and one unavailable hour at 06:00Z. Tail ran at 3% through the Oct 4 US afternoon, lifted to a 15% overnight peak by 01:00Z, decayed to 6% by 08:00Z, then oscillated between 6% and 17% through the European and US sessions as the dominant mode alternated between normal, mixed, trend-down and trend-up. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress fell from a 71% peak at 21:00Z on Oct 4 to 46% by 12:00Z before settling in the high 40s to low 50s. The 17% Tail at 14:00Z and the 9% at 16:00Z bracket the structural argument of the session: an attempted trend-up leg, a rejection, and now a resolution through it.
outlookSummary: Modelled Tail peaks at 19% in the 19:00Z power hour, where closing imbalances around a potential record print are the main conditional amplifier, then steps down to 16% at the 20:00Z settlement and into single digits through the thin evening and Asian hours. It rebuilds from 11% across the European session to 13% at the 12:30Z August balance of trade, 16% at the Oct 6 US cash open with Fed Williams at 13:05Z, and a forward peak of 17% in the first full cash hour alongside Fed Bowman at 14:45Z, before easing to 13% by 16:00Z. All 24 hours remain in the low Tail band and map to EA_ON and green. Stress stays elevated throughout, peaking at 55% around the close today and the US open tomorrow, reflecting the unresolved tension between record index levels and 24-year-high long-end yields rather than any observed one-way price path.
